subject: Hosted API latency timebox & commitment discussion for pilot
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@blueglint.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot SLOs — p50/p95 measurement windows and formal commitment

Ben —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Blueglint is keen to move forward with a 6-week pilot of Redwood Hosted for our in-product recommendations. Before we kick off procurement, legal is asking for clarifications on the latency SLOs and how you measure p50/p95 for the hosted API. A few concrete questions from our engineers and SRE: 

- Do you measure p50 and p95 per-request including streaming tokens, or do you aggregate per-client session?
- What is the measurement window for the p95 commitment? Is it a rolling 24h window, rolling 7d, or something else?
- Are there carveouts for maintenance, model rollouts, cold-starts, or regional degradation?
- If we hit a short regional degradation (e.g., 30 minutes in us-west), how does that count against the monthly SLO and any credits?

For context, our target for the in-app experience is roughly p50 <= 80ms and p95 <= 350ms for typical single-turn requests (avg payload 250 tokens). We're flexible for the pilot but need to capture the commitment shape so our product team can plan fallback logic. 

I've attached a short PDF with our expected traffic shape and payload distribution (blueglint_slo_request.pdf). Can you share a proposal for committed targets and the exact measurement semantics so we can move to an addendum?

Appreciate it —
Alex Chen
Product Lead — Recs
Blueglint Analytics

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex@blueglint.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-30T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLOs — p50/p95 measurement windows and formal commitment

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the traffic profile. Quick summary up-front: Redwood measures request latency on a per-request basis (end-to-end API call including server processing; streaming token emission is measured as time-to-first-byte for initial token and then per-token tail latency is tracked separately). For hosted API SLOs we recommend committing by two dimensions: latency target (p50/p95) and measurement timebox (how samples are bucketed and aggregated).

High-level proposal for a pilot addendum: 

Option 1 (conservative-production):
- p50: <= 70ms, p95: <= 300ms
- Measurement: rolling 30-day window, where we compute p50/p95 on 5-minute sample buckets and then aggregate daily (standard production commitment).
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows (announced >=72h), provider-level network incident (when cross-Region GCP/Azure issue is documented), and one-time model onboarding spike (first 60m after a new model variant deploy).

Option 2 (pilot-timeboxed):
- p50: <= 90ms, p95: <= 450ms
- Measurement: 14-day rolling window with p50/p95 computed on a 1-minute sample bucket then averaged across the window (timeboxed pilot behavior).
- Carveouts: same as above plus a temporary cold-start allowance for the pilot (first 2 weeks).

Notes and semantics: 
- "Sample bucket" means we compute percentiles over requests observed in each bucket (1 or 5 minute) to limit single-request noise and then aggregate those bucket percentiles across the measurement window to produce an overall metric for the window. This prevents short spikes from overwhelming a month-long commitment while still preserving tail behavior.
- Regional incidents: short region-level degradations are evaluated against the measurement window. A 30-minute degradation in one AZ will affect only the sample buckets that fall into that span; our standard credit calc uses rolling window exposure rather than a flat monthly drop. For larger incidents we use a documented incident carveout process.
- Credits / remediation: For pilot we can offer a simple remediation schedule (e.g., 5% service credit if we miss p95 in a month under Option 1 by more than 2 percentage points, escalating tiers for larger misses). Final schedule to be detailed in an addendum.

I'm looping Marissa (ops) and Rishi (SRE) to confirm the credit language and any technical carveouts. Would you prefer Option 1 (closer to production) or Option 2 (more conservative for pilot)? If you confirm, I'll draft a short addendum we can run through procurement / legal.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex@blueglint.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLOs — p50/p95 measurement windows and formal commitment

Alex / Ben —

Quick operational clarifications from our side: 

1) Measurement details we will propose in the addendum: p50/p95 computed per 1m buckets for pilot, aggregated daily, then evaluated on the selected rolling window (14-day for pilot, 30-day for production). We will explicitly exclude the following from the denominator: 
   - Requests routed to fallback model variants as a result of deliberate canarying (those are counted separately),
   - Permitted maintenance (we will supply a monthly maintenance calendar for any scheduled outages),
   - Capacity exhaustion events where an upstream provider declares a platform-level outage.

2) Cold-start carveout: For the pilot period only we will allow a cold-start carveout for the first 14 days after you onboard a new model family or change quantization profiles. This will not apply to steady-state requests.

3) Regional short-duration blips: we will treat single-region blips under 60 minutes as part of the rolling window (i.e., they count), but we will provide a remediation path (credit + joint RCA) if the incident meets our incident severity threshold.

4) Credit schedule (pilot): Miss p95 by 2–5% in a billing month -> 5% credit; 5–10% -> 10% credit; >10% -> 20% credit and optional contract review. We can refine this in the commercial addendum.

Ben: please draft the addendum language and include the explicit sample-bucket definition above. Alex: if procurement wants, we can include a 14-day trial clause that ties the pilot measurement semantics to the pilot end date (so results aren’t mixed into a later production evaluation).

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Ops — Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben / Marissa — this is helpful. Blueglint is comfortable starting the pilot on Option 2 (pilot-timeboxed) with the 14-day window and the cold-start carveout. A couple of asks before we sign: 

- Can you add a short clause that clarifies that streaming multi-chunk responses are measured by time-to-first-byte for the initial token for the SLOs (we don’t want per-token tail to be counted into the same p95 metric)?
- Please include the DocuSign link for the addendum and a HubSpot deal id so our procurement can cross-reference.
- We would like an explicit note that regional blips under 60m are not automatically eligible for credits unless they cross the severity threshold you mentioned. That language saves back-and-forth during an incident.

If you can update the draft and send the DocuSign link we can loop legal and procurement and aim to sign within 48 hours.

Best,
Alex
